chunks: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
"No one misses the prayer who intends the prayer, and the prayer of the day is not missed until the sun sets, and the prayer of the night is not missed until dawn rises."

key_terms.أَرَادَ: intended or desired, indicating purposeful resolve to perform the prayer
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, marking the limit of the nighttime prayer period mentioned here
key_terms.تَغِيبَ الشَّمْسُ: the sun sets, marking the end of the daytime prayer period mentioned here
key_terms.صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ: the nighttime prayer, meaning prayer whose time extends through the night
key_terms.صَلَاةُ النَّهَارِ: the daytime prayer, meaning prayers whose time falls within the day

ai.seo_question: Until when are the daytime and nighttime prayers considered on time in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that prayer is not considered missed so long as its time remains and a person is intent on performing it. It clarifies that daytime prayers remain within time until sunset, and nighttime prayer remains within time until the rising of dawn.
